summary.title: Writing a minimal x86-64 JIT compiler in C++ - Part 2
summary.one_liner: You learn how to wrap executable memory in a small C++ helper class and have JIT-generated x86-64 machine code call an existing C++ function.
keywords: call c++ function from generated code
takeaways: Wrap executable memory pages in a C++ class that allocates, pushes bytes and releases memory.
Use memcpy to write multi-byte values such as function addresses into generated machine code.
Call a C++ function with no arguments from JIT-generated code by embedding its address.
Use the standard function prologue and epilogue bytes when building generated functions.
Cast the generated code address to a function pointer and invoke it, observing side effects on globals.
summary.summary: The article is Part 2 of a series on building a minimal x86-64 JIT compiler in C++ for Linux or macOS. It introduces a MemoryPages struct that requests executable memory from the OS in its constructor, releases it in its destructor, and provides push functions for single bytes, multi-byte values via memcpy, and byte vectors, plus a bounds check. The author then builds a generated function that calls a C++ function test() which prints a message and modifies a global variable, using prologue and epilogue byte sequences. The program dumps the generated machine code, casts the address to a function pointer, and calls it. The full source is on a GitHub repo referenced by the article.
